Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  2-day history of midline lower abdominal (suprapubic) pain; feels hot/sweaty but self-reported temperature ~37°C (afebrile); mild nausea without vomiting; slight increase in urinary frequency; reports thirst and low fluid intake recently; noted pink-tinged urine (self-reported hematuria); no dysuria; no back pain; no abnormal urine odor; constipation last week now resolved; normal bowel movement 2 hours prior; no vaginal discharge; regular menses; no intermenstrual or postcoital bleeding; no recent travel; no similar episodes previously.
- Relevant family medical history:  Mother with breast cancer (treated).
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  No regular medications; no OTC medications reported. Allergy: amoxicillin. Past contraceptive implant (removed ~1 year ago). An antibiotic was prescribed for suspected UTI (twice daily for 3 days); specific agent/dose/route not documented.
- Immunisation status reviewed:  Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health:  Regular periods; no intermenstrual or postcoital bleeding; no vaginal discharge; prior internal contraceptive implant removed ~1 year ago; pregnancy status not discussed; no STI history recorded.
- Physical activity and nutrition:  Not recorded.
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:  Does not smoke. Alcohol ~1 beer per occasion, ~4 times/week. Other substance use not recorded.
- Hearing loss or concerns:  Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Acute onset (2 days) suprapubic pain with urinary frequency and self-reported pink urine; mild nausea; afebrile by home reading; no dysuria, no back pain, no vaginal discharge; amoxicillin allergy; no prior similar episodes.
- Impression: Features are most consistent with acute uncomplicated cystitis. Hematuria and frequency support UTI despite absence of dysuria. Distal ureteral/bladder stone remains possible given hematuria and suprapubic pain without flank pain. Pregnancy-related causes are less likely but pregnancy status was not assessed.
- Working diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated cystitis.
- Management priorities: Empiric antibiotic therapy initiated (BID x3 days; agent not documented) with safety-netting. Face-to-face review if worsening or new symptoms (fever, back pain) or if not improving.

Management Plan

- Actions/treatments: Prescribed a 3-day course of antibiotics, twice daily, sent to patient’s nominated pharmacy (specific medication not documented; amoxicillin allergy noted).
- Advice/education: Start antibiotics as soon as collected. Seek care urgently if pain worsens, fever develops, back pain occurs, new symptoms arise, or if symptoms recur.
- Follow-up: Advised to contact service for reassessment and possible face-to-face examination if not improving.
- Investigations/referrals: None performed or ordered during this consult.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Acute uncomplicated cystitis – High likelihood: Suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, and pink-tinged urine (hematuria) align; absence of dysuria does not exclude UTI; afebrile and no back pain.
- Ureterolithiasis (distal ureter/bladder neck) or bladder stone – Moderate likelihood: Hematuria with suprapubic pain and frequency; lack of flank pain/colicky pain lowers likelihood but does not exclude a distal stone.
- Early pregnancy-related condition (including ectopic) – Low likelihood: Reproductive age and lower abdominal pain warrant exclusion; regular menses and no bleeding reported; pregnancy status not assessed.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):
- Missing expected elements: BP and pulse; height/weight/BMI/waist circumference; clinician-measured temperature; urinalysis (dipstick and culture); pregnancy test; pelvic exam/CMT assessment; CVA tenderness assessment; STI risk/sexual history details; immunisation review; mental health screening; physical activity and diet history; substance use beyond alcohol/tobacco; oral/dental, ear, and vision screening; fasting glucose/lipids; cervical screening history; mammography eligibility/history.
- Internal contradictions: None noted between transcript and DDx. Potential miscommunication observed when asked about blood in stool—patient reported blood in urine; stool blood status not confirmed.
- Transcript quality: Several unclear/inaudible segments and occasional misunderstanding of questions; limited objective data and no physical exam due to telehealth format.
